newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -prices stay firm, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -prices stay firm, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices stayed firm early Tuesday afternoon, up from 1/8 to 1/4 point, but trade remained thin, looking to the Treasury market to provide clearer direction.
"We're just sitting here until something serious happens in the Treasury market," a trader said.

In the secondary market, traders focused in part on New York City bonds. The city last week sold $834 million of tax-exempt bonds, which were freed for trade late last week, but due to the U.S. Veteran's Day holiday on Monday were not moved as swiftly as they otherwise might have been.
"They're probably just catching up to the rest of the market," said another trader, explaining that the city's bonds were bid up from 1/8 to 1/4 point in some spots.

While municipal bonds now are slightly underpriced when compared with Treasuries, the mainstream of individual investors still seem to be sidelined. "Retail is coming back little by little, but it's still not beating the door down," a trader said.

While the market's recent rally might reawaken interest in more refundings, which first were proposed last Spring, only to be postponed after prices fell, traders questioned how many deals remain to be done this year.
"The rally has made room for some refunding deals...but I think it's starting to dwindle," a trader said.

As an example of the type of refunding deal now being seen, he pointed to California's State Public Works, which sold $46.7 million of lease revenue refunding bonds at a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2011.
Connecticut said that it scheduled its sale of nearly $162 million general obligation tax-exempt bonds for Wednesday.
Actively traded municipal bonds included Dade County Florida Water & Sewer System Revenues of October 2025, which were bid at 5.64 percent net and pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon.

No quotes were available from Monday due to the holiday, as also was the case for Tampa Florida Occupational License Tax Series B of October 2027, which were bid at 5.67 percent net and carry a 5-1/2 percent coupon.

The December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade rose 10 ticks to 116-31/32, lagging U.S. Treasury bond futures, which gained 17 ticks to 114-19/32. The MOB spread was 76 ticks.
